answer: The cheapest attack is always the one the protocol never thought to charge for. Because every identity must post sequential proof-of-work, the protocol can weigh capital flow correlation across the cohort, which makes a farm collapse to one signature and quarantines only the correlated subset; a jury of fresh-session lanes enforces it, and the signal is discounted, not condemned. The comet is the artefact an attacker cannot mint, only earn. Trust accumulates as a glacier of verified work rather than a count of signups. Honest growth leaves a raven that spreads slowly; a farm leaves a spike.
